title: Mixed precision fallback experiments: FP8/INT8 hybrid strategy notes
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This doc captures a set of exploratory experiments for a mixed-precision, dynamic-fallback strategy that attempts to get the cost/latency benefits of INT8/AWQ while preserving output quality for edge cases by falling back to FP8/FP16 for specific token ranges or when internal heuristics indicate risk. The goal is to produce a plausible rollout plan for a runtime feature we can A/B on Dedicated clusters.

Key ideas tested in this round:
- Hybrid encoding: use INT8 (AWQ/GPTQ-style) by default, automatically switch to FP8 when the prefix/key-value cache entropy crosses a threshold or when generation enters a high-uncertainty region (low next-token confidence).
- Per-kernel fallback: certain attention/FFN kernels executed in FP16/FP8 while matmuls remain INT8 to reduce conversion overhead while protecting numerics on critical ops.
- Short-context fastpath: for requests with <= 128 tokens, use INT8 aggressive packing w/o fallback since quality cost small; for long contexts (>1024) bias toward FP8 for KV cache stability.
- Runtime probe: inexpensive token-level confidence probe every N tokens to trigger local switch (N=16/32).

Experiment matrix (short):
- Models: Llama-2-13B-chat, MPT-7B, and a customer-provisioned 13B variant (quant-aware).
- Quant schemes: AWQ-int8, GPTQ-int8, FP8-e4m3 (operator mixed with int8), baseline FP16/FP32.
- Kernels: cuBLAS default, fused-attn (our optimized kernel), packed-matmul-v1 and v2 (two packing strategies tested).
- Workloads: short-chat (mean req len 64), long-dialog (mean len 1200, KV reuse), summarization (avg out len 320), hallucination-trigger prompts (synthetic stress tests).

Instrumentation and profiling setup:
- Wall-clock latency per token (p50/p95/p99) and end-to-end request latency.
- Throughput measured as tokens/sec under simulated QPS (1, 5, 20 concurrent sessions).
- Memory (GPU) headroom and peak allocation.
- Token-level confidence (softmax of top token) and KL to FP16 baseline distribution as a cheap proxy for quality drift.
- Quality metrics: perplexity on Wikitext2 and a small held-out summarization ROUGE-L subset; manual review of hallucination cases from stress set.
- Tracing: per-op times via CUPTI + our microtracer; track conversion copies (int8<->fp16) and cache invalidation events.

Topline findings (short):
- Latency: pure AWQ-INT8 fastpath reduces median per-token time by ~28% and p95 by ~18% vs FP16 for short-chat workloads on A100-40GB.
- Long-context instability: with aggressive INT8 for >1024 context, KL drift vs FP16 grows quickly (0.18 after 800 tokens) and hallucination rate (manual) increased ~3x on the stress set.
- Per-kernel fallback: switching just the FFN and attention accumulators to FP8 while keeping matmuls in int8 cut most instability (KL drift reduced to ~0.04 at same point) with only ~8% latency regression from pure int8 fastpath.
- Probe heuristic: confidence-probe (N=16) correctly flagged ~85% of tokens that later diverged significantly; costs ~0.6% throughput.
- Kernel packing: packed-matmul-v2 improved memory locality and reduced conversion overhead; combined with per-kernel fallback gave best cost/quality tradeoff.

Representative numbers (Llama-2-13B-chat on A100-40GB, short-chat workload):
- FP16 baseline: p50 token 12.8ms, p95 20.4ms, throughput 420 tokens/s, GPU mem 28.1GB.
- AWQ-INT8 fastpath: p50 token 9.2ms, p95 16.7ms, throughput 580 tokens/s, GPU mem 22.7GB.
- Hybrid per-kernel (matmul int8, FFN/attn accum FP8): p50 9.9ms, p95 17.5ms, throughput 540 tokens/s, GPU mem 24.1GB.
- FP8-all (naive): p50 11.5ms, p95 18.9ms, throughput 470 tokens/s, GPU mem 25.0GB.
- Notes: conversion copies are the main overhead when toggling; keeping memory layout stable avoids 60-120us spikes per toggle.

Quality summary (Wikitext perplexity and ROUGE-L on summarization subset):
- FP16 baseline: PPL 12.6, ROUGE-L 41.2
- AWQ-INT8: PPL 14.9 (+18%), ROUGE-L 39.0 (-5.4%)
- Hybrid per-kernel: PPL 13.1 (+4%), ROUGE-L 40.5 (-1.7%)
- FP8-all: PPL 12.9 (+2.4%), ROUGE-L 40.9 (-0.7%)
- Manual stress hallucination rate (synthetic set): baseline 2.1%, AWQ-int8 6.8%, hybrid 2.9%, FP8-all 2.6%

Observations and root-cause analysis notes:
- INT8 activations/weights are generally fine for local token generation in short contexts, but the KV cache accumulation amplifies small quant errors over long contexts. Attn softmax and FFN residual scaling are hot spots.
- FP8 accumulator for attention/FFN captures the majority of numeric stability benefit with minimal perf cost. This matches float16 literature where accumulators are more important than operand precision for iterative accumulation-heavy ops.
- Conversion overhead: format toggles (layout changes) are much worse than conversion math. Keeping a stable in-memory int8 layout and doing a per-op on-GPU cast is cheaper than swap-and-repack. Packed kernels that accept int8 with native bias offsets avoid expensive repacks.
- Probe heuristic false positives: some probes flip to FP8 for tokens that would have been fine in int8 — this mainly happens on nouns/entities where token entropy drops but the model picks a rare token. We can reduce this by combining probe with delta-KL over last 8 tokens instead of raw confidence.

Operational considerations for rollout:
- Canary policy: enable hybrid per-kernel fallback on 5% of Dedicated customers (lowest-risk) for a week with traffic sharding by model-route and request size. Monitor p50/p95 latency and KL proxy.
- Metrics to gate: user-facing error/hallucination alerts (customer-reported), ROUGE/PPL regressions on sampled evals, p95 latency increase >10% for route.
- Cost modeling: hybrid approach trades ~6-9% throughput vs AWQ-int8 but reduces predicted hallucination-related incident cost by an order of magnitude for long-context apps. For short-chat apps default AWQ-int8 might still be best.

Implementation notes / prototype decisions:
- Kernel changes required: expose per-op accumulation dtype flags, add lightweight on-device cast helpers, and implement packed-matmul-v2 path that accepts int8 with stride flags. Avoid global model re-quantization at runtime.
- Config knobs: context-length threshold, probe interval (N tokens), KL threshold, per-route override (customers can lock to FP16/FP8/INT8).
- Tracing: add a histogram of fallback events per-request and record conversion bytes to make toggles debuggable.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Test on H100 and lower-memory GPUs (L40/RTX6000) — performance/overhead tradeoffs differ and FP8 hardware support matters.
- Evaluate with more models (70B-like) where accumulation error might be more or less critical.
- Tune probe heuristics: try combined delta-KL + entropy + recent-token perplexity; explore learned probe classifier (small logistic regressor trained on previous toggles).
- Investigate whether small amount of selective retraining / calibration (per-route) can shift kernels to be more int8-robust without full GPTQ/awq pipeline.

Action items (owners):
- Ben T: implement packed-matmul-v2 accept-int8 path + trace metrics (due 2026-09-24).
- Clara L: run H100 small-batch suite and report variance (due 2026-09-20).
- Asha N: prototype probe classifier dataset and baseline logistic model (due 2026-09-30).
- Product: pick 2 candidate Dedicated routes for 5% canary by 2026-09-22.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is exploratory and intentionally fuzzy in some thresholds. Focus review on feasibility of kernel changes and whether the canary gating makes sense operationally.
- I attached a quick trace sample (see linked PR) that shows fallback spikes — worth reviewing to confirm the conversion cost estimates.

Appendix (brief):
- Example fallback timeline trace excerpt: token 0-128 int8 fast, token 144 probe triggered (KL > 0.075), at t=4.1s we flip FFN->FP8 accumulate, conversion adds 110us spike, subsequent tokens stable and KL reduces by 0.03. Toggle back at token 208 when delta-KL < 0.01 for 32 tokens.
- Small checklist for A/B: enable tracing, sample 0.1% of responses for ROUGE eval, maintain incident playbook for rollback (route-level).

End.
